name: Reporting burden

subjectOf.text: Requiring hedge funds to supply risk and valuation data in a simplified format would in fact impose a significant burden on the industry, since simplification requirements would raise transaction costs, require pre-screening, and possibly additional staff.
subjectOf.abstract: In addition to the utilization problem, if the SEC should require hedge funds to provide risk and valuation data in a certain simplified format, the SEC would in fact impose a significant burden on the hedge fund industry.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387
scope_conditions: where the SEC prescribes a simplified reporting format

subjectOf.text: Form PF is structured so that single strategy fund advisers collect and provide only a fraction of the information a multi strategy adviser must make available, which makes reporting burden a function of strategy count rather than of adviser size.
subjectOf.abstract: Form PF is structured in a way that allows single strategy fund advisers to collect and provide a fraction of the information a multi strategy adviser would be required to make available under Form PF.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Impact of Dodd-Frank Act Compliance Cost on the Hedge Fund Industry (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389423
scope_conditions: comparison of single strategy and multi strategy advisers

subjectOf.text: Because Form PF requires less information from single strategy advisers, hedge fund advisers that apply only a single strategy to their portfolios may incur overall lower compliance cost.
subjectOf.abstract: Accordingly, hedge fund advisers that apply only a single strategy to their respective portfolios may incur overall lower compliance cost.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Impact of Dodd-Frank Act Compliance Cost on the Hedge Fund Industry (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389423
scope_conditions: advisers using a single investment strategy
Title IV and Form PF compliance

subjectOf.text: Form PF required disclosures of counterparty credit exposure constitute sensitive information that individual fund managers often cannot readily determine, which makes that reporting requirement hard to satisfy.
subjectOf.abstract: For instance, Form PF required disclosures of counterparty credit exposure constitute sensitive information that often cannot be readily determined by the individual fund managers.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: Form PF counterparty credit exposure items

subjectOf.text: Some Form PF disclosure requirements are not answerable as designed, because counterparty credit exposure is sensitive information that individual private fund managers often cannot readily determine.
subjectOf.abstract: For instance, the disclosure of counterparty credit exposure is sensitive information that often cannot readily be determined by the individual private investment fund managers.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Investment Fund Regulation - Theory and Empirical Evidence from 1998 to 2016 (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2998097
scope_conditions: Form PF counterparty credit exposure items
